The Jagersfontein disaster

By: Sinethemba Nogude | Paid

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Its a disaster many say could have been prevented...With at least 4 people dead ,we visit a community that this is in shock and still reeling.

Unique Selling Point:
Its a lazy Sunday morning in Jagersfontein, residents are waking, preparing to go church others to run their errands before Monday...but little did they know they were minutes from disaster. ... A dam in the abandoned Jagersfontein diamond mine collapsed early Sunday, triggering heavy flooding that damaged property and killed at least three people.

About nine houses were swept away and more than 20 damaged by flood waters after the dam wall of the historic mine collapsed.

JAGERSFONTEIN is home to the oldest and largest diamond mine hole in the world. Mining began in 1870 and the pit was hand-dug for 39 years until 1909. Due to the Great Depression, the mine closed in the early 1930s and reopened in the late 1940s. Thereafter it remained in service until 1973, when the operation – then owned by De Beers – was finally shut down.

For many years, mine workers migrated between the diamond mines in Jagersfontein and the nearby town of Koffiefontein. These towns are now home to many retired mine workers and their families.

The Jagersfontein Diamond Mine and tailings were originally owned by the diamond producer De Beers. The tailings were then sold to Jagersfontein Developments (Pty) Ltd, which is recovering diamonds from the tailings.

We look at the aftermath of this tragic event, as communities pick up the pieces of their lives and As South Africa poses the question: Who was responsible, and could this disaster have been prevented?

Script:


l
Upsounds Visuals

Opening :






V/O A 100 KM south of Bloemfontein in the Free state lies the sleepy town of Jagersfontein

Link : Its just before 6 o'clock , Sunday the 11th 2022, and the residents of Jagersfontein have no idea what is about to befall them

V/O Moments later the dam used to store water and waste from the mine here- known as a tailings dam was about change their lives.

Upsound victim Lindile:I heard rumbling, I thought it was rain.I ignored It and I slept again.

Upsound victim Thami: I heard the noise and opened the windows and curtains . It wasn't the wind, it wasn’t the rain.















Dramatic cellphone footage
Link : At 6, the tailings dam burst sending a deadly mudslide directly towards the community here located just a few meters away.

V/O Terrified onlookers captured the devastation.

V/O Once a thriving diamond mining town in the late 1800s, Jagersfontein had seen better days by the time the De Beers mine shut down in 1973

V/OBut in 2010 a sense of optimism swept through the area when a mining company - Jagersfontein Developments rolled into town, reprocessing the old mine dumps, known as tailings, from the original excavation.

V/O Leaving the ever-expanding mine tailings dam ominously looming over the town.

Upsound Lindile : I woke up and went outside I realised the dam had broken.

V/O Lindile Saula was one of the first people to witness the dam's collapse.

Upsound Lindile It became dark,there was dust and a loud sound.It came like the ocean

Upsound Lindile I dropped everything and ran outside, when I was running, I called out to my neighbors to run.
V/O 300 meters away his neighbor Thamsanqa Mokgwane was still trying to get his wife and son to safety.
Upsound Thami : My wife and kid were sleeping , “I said please wake up”.
Upsound Thami By the time my son got out the gate , the water was this high.I grabbed him and helped him over the fence.
V/O 1,5 million cubic liters of mine waste in the form of sand, mud and water, was hurtling through the community.
Upsound Dr Charles MacRobert it's. Probably the size of a small hill cascading down on the community in a very watery form. So it's it's a huge amount of material.
V/O Geotechnical Engineer Dr. Charles MacRobert has studied the disaster.
Upsound : it's got a high smectite content, which is just the type of clay, so it's not toxic per se, but it's just very mobile and it can be very destructive.
Upsound Lindile : It hit everything once and swept everything, that’s what happened to our houses .We lost everything.

V/O Just a few kilometers away Farmer Albertus van Staden received a desperate plea for help.
Upsound Albertus :Just after 7 the neighbor sent me a message saying the dam wall broke and I must come and help.
Upsound :I then phoned the neighbors who are further down, downstream, and told them to get their animals out of the wa, and to pull out their pumps.
Upsound Albertus : We were a little too late, it happened too fast. And then the water that came down here, the “sludge”, covered the sheep. We couldn’t save them all.
Upsound Albertus :It wasn’t only animals it was also people. We got two people here that the mud brought here, just here in the veld.

Upsound Jandre : I got the, the message probably around about just after 8.
Upsound Jandre : We just know there was a tailings dam that collapsed and from that, you know, the devastation can be very dramatic.
V/O As the news of the disaster filtered across the country, Director of independent mine monitoring company TSF Risk Solutions Jandre de Wet assembled a team to assist in the rescue efforts and damage assessment.

V/O The devastation was overwhelming.
Upsound Jandre de Wet : I was quite taken aback What was something for me was an astounding signing off on a foundation of a house that was completely stripped away. That was quite, quite eye-opening to me.
Upsound Jandre de wet :We did a reconnaissance of the area ,there was still reports of a , missing lady.
V/OThat woman was one of several people missing that morning

Upsound Thami 4: My neighbour, she was standing in front of a shack when I ran, I heard she was swept away. They are still looking for her body.
Upsound Claire : What happened to your neighbour ?
Upsound Lindile: Monday we heard that forensics confirmed that the old man had died.

Breather

UPSOUND MARIUS: It was in the southeastern corner. Well, actually in the middle. Okay. In the southern part where there was a collapse and it was not a break.

V/OJagersfontein Developments Legal Compliance officer Marius de Villiers says he is still baffled by the collapse.


Upsound Marius : It was it seems as if there was a sagging of the wall on one side. And that's where I want to say, you know, that I won't be able to determine why that occurred.

Upsound MacRobert : there's probably two levels of what went wrong this what went wrong physically on the morning and is that is what went wrong before that.
Upsound Dr Charles MacRobert :So tailings dams are inanimate.They don't make decisions to fail. And so so people take decisions within a knowledge base to prevent failure.
V/O By 12 PM that Sunday, the extent of the damage was clear. The mudslide had left the town reeling, with no power or water … over 250 people were displaced, houses had been swept away and roads flooded. 1 person was confirmed dead, whilst 3 more were unaccounted for.

Upsound Corene GOTG : 0:16 Sunday the community started calling us in distress, and we immediately despatched our teams for all over.

VO: Later that morning Gift of the Givers coordinator Corene Conradie started to receive desperate calls.
Upsound Corene 1:46 No one had drinking water …Nobody could get out ,nobody could enter until most of the sludge was clear…when we arrived with the water people started to drink immediately.The other need is personal higiene items , its ofcourse food, its matrasses
Upsound Corene : Electricity is off in all of these areas people are making fires to prepare their food.
Link Claire : In the Aftermath of this deadly disaster communities are left to pick up the pieces ,hundreds have been affected and homes obliterated ,what stings is the thought that this catastrophe could have been avoided.

V/O Reports would come out that 2 years prior the Free State provincial government ordered the company to cease operations for exceeding their authorized storage limits…
and that the Water department of water affairs issued a warning to stabilize.Walls of the dam.
Upsound Dr charles MacRobert: it is something that is foremost in our minds, is to prevent this type of failure and if we look back at a lot of failures, we often see that it's not a full understanding of the science behind the problem, but just a failure to implement or make good decisions.

Upsound Lindile : We told them that the dam is not safe. We told the managers of the mines for 4 to 5 years.

VO: De Villiers claims the community has never raised concerns about the stability of the dam with Jagersfontein Developments.


Upsound Marius : it's never been raised
Upsound Claire LThe concerns around the dam has never been raised ?

Upsound Marius: Not, not. As far as I'm concerned. That was raised to me personally.


Upsound Claire :Some people have lost everything, including family members. What would you say to them?

Upsound Marius:I understand and I understand the position.But I think if we look at what the mine and Jagersfontein developments and for instance, the trust, which is a trust belonging
is for the benefit of the community has done over the last ten, 12 years. I think that's unfounded.

VO: He says reports that the dam was too full and over-flowed, leading to erosion and collapse of the dam, are incorrect.

Upsound :I think now at this stage when the break occurred, I think the freeboard was in the region of about five meters, so well within.


V/O A Freeboard is the vertical distance from the surface of the water to the top of the dam and should always be closely monitered.


Claire : So it was the integrity or the structural integrity of the dam that was compromised? If you saying that the freeboard was five meters.



Upsound Marius I'm not going to speculate about that.
VO: Jagersfontein Developments has allocated R20 million towards the relief effort and De Villiers promises that there will be a thorough investigation

Claire :Do you take responsibility for what has happened ?

Upsound Marius 13:11:23:21 - 13:11:49:13>
Well, we as a company, you know, responsibility is I mean, if we are the owners, we are responsible, but obviously, it all depends what the position is with what happened. And that's what we are trying to establish.




VO: Aerial footage shows that the grey slime has washed many kilometers downstream from the dam, causing environmental damage that is yet to be counted.


Upsound Albertus: there is about a thousand hectares under sludge. And further downstream, there are a lot of farmers. There is an irrigation farmer who cannot irrigate because of the sludge.

Upsound Claire : Could this have been prevented?

Upsound Marius I haven't got an answer for you on that part ,I cant qualify it.

Upsound Claire :People say if you have to qualify, then the answer is yes.

Upsound Mariu:s The answer is, I don't know.


V/O For now the all that the residents of Jagersfonten can do is to pick up is to pick up the pieces of their lives and salvage what they can




[ end]

metadata.Unique Selling Point: Its a lazy Sunday morning in Jagersfontein, residents are waking, preparing to go church others to run their errands before Monday...but little did they know they were minutes from disaster. ... A dam in the abandoned Jagersfontein diamond mine collapsed early Sunday, triggering heavy flooding that damaged property and killed at least three people. About nine houses were swept away and more than 20 damaged by flood waters after the dam wall of the historic mine collapsed. JAGERSFONTEIN is home to the oldest and largest diamond mine hole in the world. Mining began in 1870 and the pit was hand-dug for 39 years until 1909. Due to the Great Depression, the mine closed in the early 1930s and reopened in the late 1940s. Thereafter it remained in service until 1973, when the operation – then owned by De Beers – was finally shut down. For many years, mine workers migrated between the diamond mines in Jagersfontein and the nearby town of Koffiefontein. These towns are now home to many retired mine workers and their families. The Jagersfontein Diamond Mine and tailings were originally owned by the diamond producer De Beers. The tailings were then sold to Jagersfontein Developments (Pty) Ltd, which is recovering diamonds from the tailings. We look at the aftermath of this tragic event, as communities pick up the pieces of their lives and As South Africa poses the question: Who was responsible, and could this disaster have been prevented?
